newsitem.title: USA: Lehman starts Trenwick, cites M&A,buybacks.
newsitem.headline: Lehman starts Trenwick, cites M&A,buybacks.

text.p: Lehman Brothers said analyst Peter Wade started coverage of Trenwick Group Inc with an outperform rating, citing expectations for share buybacks and deal activity, including a possible sale of the company.
"We believe Trenwick is exploring all opportunities available to it, including mergers, acquisitions and an outright sale of the company," Wade said in a research report.
The company was not immediately available for comment.
Wade said in the report he expects any acquisition to be positive for shareholders because of management's oppposition to deals that would be dilutive to earnings.

"Regarding a sale of the company, we believe management is likely looking for an offer around $45, but we believe may be willing to accept an offer in the low $40 range given their bearish outlook on the reinsurance market," he wrote in the report.
Typically, he said, reinsurers with Trenwick's characteristics have been acquired at about 1.5 times book value per share, which would be about $41 a share.
In addition, he said, he expects Trenwick to return a significant portion of its capital to investors through share repurchases.
He said the firm has about $60 million in cash left over from the proceeds of its trust preferred securities, which he said is likely to be used for share repurchases in 1997.
This, he said, should enable Trenwick to repurchase almost 10 percent of its outstanding shares.
Wade said he set a one-year price target of $37 for Trenwick and estimates 1997 earnings at $3.20 a share and 1998 earnings at $3.60 a share.
